name: siddiqian-plugins
description: Claude Code plugins: gitflow enforcement, repository governance, changelog upkeep, delivery discipline, a global brief-mode switch, approval-first working, quick hotfixes, session handoffs and contributor onboarding.

plugins.name: gitflow-guard
plugins.description: Enforces gitflow where the work happens. Hard-denies commits and pushes on protected branches before git runs, cuts feature branches from dev so ancestry is right by construction, and tracks the feature lifecycle against your plan.

plugins.name: repo-governance
plugins.description: Code-owner review and push detection for repositories that cannot use branch protection. Replaces the GitHub features a private repo on the Free plan does not get, and audits what is actually in force.

plugins.name: delivery-discipline
plugins.description: Three habits that keep delivered work honest: end every task with manual verification steps that separate what was run from what still needs running, never write a claim that is not traceable to code, and enforce the project's vocabulary in code as well as documents.

plugins.name: changelog-keeper
plugins.description: Turns Conventional Commits into Keep a Changelog entries. Reminds rather than generates, because changelog entries are curated prose, and gates the pull request when a notable change lands with no entry.

plugins.name: brief-mode
plugins.description: A global switch that treats every prompt as if it began with "be brief:". Start a prompt with "exp:" for a full answer to that one message; toggle with /brief-mode:on and /brief-mode:off.

plugins.name: seek-approval
plugins.description: Before acting on an instruction or building anything, settle what it means and get every consequential decision approved: atomic points, exactly four real options per question, recommended first with the why, and an adversarial grill on the options and on the approved set. Includes grill-me for hard pushback on any idea.

plugins.name: quick-hotfix
plugins.description: One small fix while you test live: a test budget, a static-check level, a scope lock and a security floor that never moves. A frontend-only variant refuses anything outside the UI, and two variants run seek-approval on the instruction first.

plugins.name: session-handoff
plugins.description: One session per feature: end a session by writing what the next one needs that is not in the code, the git log or memory, and start the next by reading it, verifying it against the world and deleting it so it cannot go stale.

plugins.name: contributor-onboarding
plugins.description: "Onboard me": finds the project's own setup declaration (.claude/onboarding.md, else CONTRIBUTING or a setup script), runs it in report mode, explains each gap, fixes what the clone can fix with the person's go, and separates what only another person can give, such as host access or credentials.
